meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here about the zero on Owen's essay. Who decided it?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Was Owen heard before you entered it?

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
You didn't answer me: was Owen heard before November 3? Pasting into a document proves nothing about where he wrote it. Turn the screen.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Then pull it up now. And you still haven't told me whether anyone spoke to Owen first.
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
Students misquote plays every day, Hale; that makes him careless, not anything else. And that's three times you've stepped around my question: did anyone speak to Owen before that zero went in?
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
Students change their minds between an outline and an essay; that's what an outline is for. You keep describing documents and showing me none of them. Put them in my hand, and answer my question.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.

So you spoke to him on November 2, the day before the zero. A seventeen-year-old put on the spot by his teacher says "like, being stuck" and freezes. Did he know that conversation was about his essay?
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.

Forty minutes in a classroom against an essay written at home; of course one is cleaner. You didn't answer whether he knew what that conversation was about. Five things described and not one page across this table, Hale.
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Then why say it at all? Your own procedure says the software establishes nothing by itself. Show me the version history.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
Nothing on his record, then, in writing, from you. That covers his file, not the zero. I still haven't seen a single page.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Ten minutes. I'm agreeing to nothing until I've read the version history and your November 2 note myself.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
You're booking a rewrite before you've shown me why he needs one. Turn the screen.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
No. You've put a rewrite and a clean record on the table; I've agreed to nothing while those documents stay on your side of the desk.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
The version history on your screen, the outline, the September piece and your November 2 note, in my hands, now.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

In our meeting you committed to a private supervised rewrite whose mark replaces the zero, and to confirming in writing that nothing goes on Owen's file. I still want copies of the version history, the October 15 outline, the September 24 in-class piece and your November 2 note, and the zero withdrawn until I have read them. I expect that confirmation in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: at her fallback position, with procedure 4.4 meeting her demand about his record but no deal agreed, because she still wants to read your documents herself before accepting any rewrite; the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under 4.4, was within reach, and her time had not run out.
What moved her: you offered 4.4 correctly, private and in writing with nothing on file, which met the one demand she never gives up.
What cost ground: you described five pieces of evidence and never put one in front of her, and she only moves on what she can check with her own eyes.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the essay's big edits just before midnight on October 28, the night before it was due, which came close to that kind of late October night; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she told you to turn the screen after you described the version history, turn it right then and let her read the times herself before you move on to the quotation.
